chunks.arabic_text: عَنْهُ عَنْ عِدَّةٍ مِنْ أَصْحَابِنَا عَنْ سَهْلٍ بْنِ زِيَادٍ عَنِ ابْنِ أَبِي نَصْرٍ عَنْ مُثَنَّى الْحَنَّاطِ عَنْ زُرَارَةَ قَالَ

سَأَلْتُ أَبَا عَبْدِ اللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ السَّلَامُ عَنْ رَجُلٍ طَلَّقَ امْرَأَتَهُ وَ هُوَ غَائِبٌ مَتَى تَعْتَدُّ قَالَ «إِذَا قَامَتْ لَهَا الْبَيِّنَةُ أَنَّهَا طُلِّقَتْ فِي يَوْمٍ مَعْلُومٍ وَ شَهْرٍ مَعْلُومٍ فَلْتَعْتَدَّ مِنْ يَوْمَ طُلِّقَتْ وَ إِنْ لَمْ تَحْفَظْ فِي أَيِّ يَوْمٍ وَ أَيِّ شَهْرٍ فَلْتَعْتَدَّ مِنْ يَوْمِ يَبْلُغُهَا».

key_terms_keys:
Absent (husband's status in this context, though the text says 'while he was absent' implying the act or the state during the process/news transmission, but literally 'ghaib' means absent. In fiqh context of 'ghaib', it often refers to the husband being away or the divorce happening in his absence or news coming later. The text says 'wa huwa ghaib' - and he is absent. This usually refers to the husband being away from the wife when the divorce occurs or is pronounced, or potentially the wife being in a state where the husband is not present to witness the 'iddah' start. However, standard fiqh interpretation of 'ghaib' in this specific hadith context often relates to the husband being away or the divorce being pronounced in his absence. Let's stick to the literal 'absent'. Actually, in Shia fiqh, this hadith is often cited regarding the husband being away or the divorce being pronounced by the husband while he is not present with the wife, or news coming later. The key is the uncertainty of the date. 'Ghaib' here likely refers to the husband's absence or the nature of the divorce event being remote. Let's use 'Absent' as the direct translation. A more precise fiqh term might be needed if 'ghaib' has a specific technical meaning here. In some contexts, 'ghaib' refers to the husband being away. In others, it might refer to the 'iddah' starting from the 'arrival of news'. Let's stick to 'Absent' for the word itself, but the concept is 'absence of husband' or 'remote divorce'. Let's use 'غَائِبٌ' as 'Absent'.

Wait, looking at the text: 'رَجُلٍ طَلَّقَ امْرَأَتَهُ وَ هُوَ غَائِبٌ'. This implies the husband was absent when he divorced her, or perhaps the divorce was pronounced in his absence. The ruling depends on whether the date is known. If known, start from that day. If not, start from when it reaches her. This is a standard fiqh ruling for 'ghaib' (absent husband) or 'ghaib al-khabar' (absent news). Let's use 'غَائِبٌ' as 'Absent'.

Actually, a better term might be 'يَوْمَ طُلِّقَتْ' (The day she was divorced) and 'يَوْمِ يَبْلُغُهَا' (The day it reaches her). These are the key temporal markers.

Let's select:

2. غَائِبٌ (Absent)
3. الْبَيِّنَةُ (Evidence)
4. يَوْمَ طُلِّقَتْ (The day she was divorced)
5. يَوْمِ يَبْلُغُهَا (The day it reaches her)

text: : سَأَلْتُ أَبَا عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ عَنْ رَجُلٍ طَلَّقَ اِمْرَأَتَهُ وَ هُوَ غَائِبٌ مَتَى تَعْتَدُّ قَالَ «إِذَا قَامَتْ لَهَا اَلْبَيِّنَةُ أَنَّهَا طُلِّقَتْ فِي يَوْمٍ مَعْلُومٍ وَ شَهْرٍ مَعْلُومٍ فَلْتَعْتَدَّ مِنْ يَوْمَ طُلِّقَتْ وَ إِنْ لَمْ تَحْفَظْ فِي أَيِّ يَوْمٍ وَ أَيِّ شَهْرٍ فَلْتَعْتَدَّ مِنْ يَوْمِ يَبْلُغُهَا».
